newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Senior Russian official shot dead in St Petersburg.
newsitem.headline: Senior Russian official shot dead in St Petersburg.

text.p: A sniper shot dead the deputy governor of Russia's second city, St Petersburg, on Monday, the mayor's office said in a statement.

Mikhail Manevich, 36, was travelling with his wife in a car when eight shots from an automatic rifle, apparently equipped with a telescopic sight, penetrated the roof of his vehicle, killing him and slightly wounding his wife, it said.
"It is not excluded that the killer was shooting from an attic of a building," a Federal Security Service spokesman told Reuters.
The building from where the shots were fired is on the corner of the Nevsky Prospekt, St Petersburg's busiest shopping street.

Manevich headed the State Property Committee -- responsible for real estate -- in St Petersburg. He was one of the few officials who remained in office after mayor Vladimir Yakovlev ousted his liberal predecessor Anatoly Sobchak.
The mayor has governor status and a seat in the Federation Council upper house of parliament.
Graft scandals, some involving real estate sales, have rocked St Petersburg over the past two years.
Killings of businessmen, industrialists and even state officials are not uncommon in Russia, where hundreds of Mafia-style criminal gangs are fighting for influence.
